name: Happeo
tagline: An intranet and internal comms platform built around Google Workspace, with pages, channels, and federated search.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Happeo is sales-led with quoted pricing rather than a public monthly number.

verdictSummary: An intranet has exactly one job: be the place everyone in the company already looks. A personal, self-hosted version of that is a wiki with a lonely announcements tab. The buildable part, pages plus a feed plus full text search, is genuinely a weekend of work; the unbuildable part is Google Workspace SSO, group-derived permissions, Drive and Calendar federation, audit trails, and the org chart that makes any of it navigable. Happeo also sells the boring enterprise wrapper: retention, access reviews, admin governance, someone to call when search breaks. If you are one person, you do not want this product, you want a notes app.
coreLoopDIY: Spins up a local Markdown wiki with an announcement feed, tags, and SQLite full text search over both, all in one repo.
requirements: a server or container if more than one person uses it
Markdown files or a willingness to paste content in
a Google Cloud OAuth client if you want even basic Google sign-in
whatYouLose: Google Workspace SSO and permissions that follow existing groups, so access control becomes one shared password or nothing
Federated search across Drive, Calendar, and third-party tools; your search only knows what you typed into it
Publishing workflow: drafts, approvals, expiry dates, mandatory-read tracking, reach analytics
Admin governance, audit logs, retention policies, and the compliance paperwork enterprises actually buy
Mobile apps, push notifications, and the Google Workspace sidebar placement that gets people to open it at all
moatNotes: Deep Google Workspace coupling is both the moat and the ceiling: it is very hard to rebuild and only matters if your company lives in Workspace.
whyPeopleStillPay: Companies pay because the alternative is a Drive folder nobody can find things in and a Slack channel that scrolls away. What Happeo sells is not the page editor, it is the guarantee that the intranet inherits the identity system, respects existing group permissions, searches across the tools people already use, and survives an IT security review. None of that is interesting engineering, all of it is expensive to own. A solo builder gets no value from any of it, which is why this entry is a no rather than a challenge.
notes: You can build the wiki in a weekend; you cannot build the fact that everyone opens it. The moat is Google Workspace identity and permissions inheritance plus the enterprise governance layer bolted on top.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted internal wiki and announcements board for a very small team. This is the honest consolation prize for a company intranet, not a clone of one.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15, App Router, TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/app.db
- Tailwind CSS, no component library
- Markdown stored in the database, rendered server side with remark plus rehype-sanitize

Data model:
- pages: id, slug, title, body_md, tags (comma string), updated_at, updated_by
- posts: id, title, body_md, author, pinned (bool), created_at
- revisions: id, page_id, body_md, created_at, author (append only, no diff UI needed)
- an FTS5 virtual table indexing page titles, page bodies, post titles, post bodies

Features that are in scope:
- Home page: pinned posts first, then the feed newest first, then a sidebar list of recently edited pages
- Wiki: /wiki/[slug] renders a page, /wiki/[slug]/edit is a plain textarea with live preview, saving writes a revision row
- Create page from a 404 state, so broken links are the way you author
- Tag index at /tags/[tag]
- Search at /search that queries FTS5 across pages and posts, snippets highlighted, results grouped by type
- Single shared password from AUTH_PASSWORD in .env, checked in middleware, stored as an httpOnly signed cookie. Name from a display-name cookie, no user accounts
- npm run seed creates a handful of example pages and posts so the UI is not empty

Explicitly out of scope, do not build these:
- OAuth, SSO, Google Workspace integration, per-user or per-group permissions
- Comments, reactions, notifications, email digests, mobile apps
- Analytics, telemetry, any outbound network calls at all
- File uploads and rich text editors; Markdown and pasted image URLs only

Secrets in .env only, .env.example committed, real .env gitignored. Ship a README with setup in five lines or fewer and a one line note that this has no access control beyond one shared password.
